undeclared amendment: M4 says a reading of `stuck` or `needs-human` with any other message appends `driver:attention` exactly as at BASE with the one added field, but the new `attentionUnwritten` set in `fleet/run-engine.mjs` (`if (value === 'needs-human') attentionUnwritten.delete(taskId)

else if (attentionUnwritten.has(taskId)) return`) suppresses EVERY non-`needs-human` reading of a task whose note-raised patch the hub refused — including a genuine worker writing `work.attention: stuck` with its own message. The set exists for a real reason (after a refused patch the hub still reads `ok`, and recording that would put a hand-lowering nobody performed on the record every poll), and M3's refusal branch is exactly the state that creates it, so this is not a defect in what the exam drives — but the narrowing is wider than the problem, and no AMENDMENTS entry declares it. Narrowing the suppression to the `ok` echo alone keeps M3's refusal branch working and leaves M4's clause whole.

`notesPoll` runs on a `setInterval` callback that discards its promise (`setInterval(() => { notesPoll() }, attentionPollMs)`), and its body has a `try/finally` with no `catch` around `for (const ev of rows) await notesReadEvent(ev)`. BASE's `attentionRead` — the same shape, on the same timer — wraps its whole body in `try { … } catch { }` precisely because a timer has nowhere to throw to: a rejection here is an unhandled rejection out of the engine, not a poll that learned nothing. The reachable paths are narrow today (`readNote` never rejects, `kata.getIssue` is already in a try, `appendEvent` swallows its own write failure, and `kataFatal` is only ever constructed by the engine at the dispatch revision check, so `kataCall` inside `notesRaiseHand` cannot rethrow against a real client), but the global constraint that a Jev-lane failure is 'never a thrown error out of the engine' is one line of defence away.
